claims.text: The starting material is selective-laser-melted Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
The as-printed alloy is more than 97% dense.
The as-printed alloy has a single-fcc cellular microstructure.
The as-printed alloy has a uniform Cr distribution and no nanoprecipitates.
Aging at 750°C for 50 h generates approximately 25–30 vol% nanoprecipitates.
The aged alloy contains Ni/Ti-enriched L12 and Al/Ti-enriched L21 nanoprecipitates.
The L21 precipitates are larger and depleted in Cr and Fe.
The dual nanoprecipitates are predominantly localized near cell walls.
Formation of the dual nanoprecipitates locally depletes Cr in the matrix and at precipitate–matrix interfaces.
Localized Cr depletion delays or impedes early formation of a continuous protective Cr2O3 scale.
Precipitate–matrix interfaces provide short-circuit paths for oxygen diffusion.
Uniform Cr in the as-printed alloy facilitates outward Cr diffusion and rapid formation of a continuous Cr2O3 scale.
The continuous Cr2O3 scale in the as-printed alloy restricts further oxidation.
Delayed Cr2O3 formation in the aged alloy permits greater oxygen penetration and reaction with Al and Ti.
The aged alloy develops a mixed duplex-to-trilayer oxide scale containing an inner Al/Ti-rich layer.
The aged alloy will exhibit greater oxidation mass gain than the as-printed alloy, especially above approximately 900°C.
The as-printed and aged states will have similar activation energies for oxide growth.
The aged alloy will develop a thicker and less protective inner Al/Ti-rich oxide layer.
The protective effect of the as-printed alloy's Cr2O3 scale is effective primarily below approximately 900°C.
The precipitate-associated increase in oxidation should be observable above 900°C within 96 h.

contradictions.description: The intervention describes the L21 precipitates themselves as Cr-depleted, while the mediator asserts that their formation depletes Cr from the surrounding matrix and interfaces. Cr-depleted precipitates would ordinarily reject rather than consume Cr, so an additional segregation or transport explanation is needed to reconcile these statements.
